Ethan: Hey folks — heads up: planning to work from Phuket, Thailand for ~90 days (May 15 - Aug 13). Quick Qs: will I get WFH stipend pro-rated? Any payroll/tax steps? Health insurance coverage? Need approval or anything else? cc @people-ops
Priya (People Ops): Thanks @Ethan! Quick checklist: please submit the Geo Move Request form (https://redwood.example.com/policies/geo-move-request), update Homebase with temporary location, and attach dates + local address. Stipend is usually pro-rated for trips >30 days; I'll confirm the exact calc. Payroll/tax will need to review for Thailand.
Liam (Payroll): Adding payroll context — for a 90-day stay in Thailand we typically don't do a payroll cutover. However we need to confirm withholding rules and ADP location flags. Q: will you be doing any client-facing or revenue-generating activities while there?
Ethan: No client-facing work locally, mostly writing, async work, and meetings with US folks. I'll keep my US bank account and payroll info. I plan to enter on a tourist visa and extend locally if needed.
Priya (People Ops): Visa is personal responsibility; company policy requires you not to work in a way that violates local visa terms. We also need an emergency contact and a local address for any benefit shipments. Stipend pro-ration approach: monthly WFH allowance * (days abroad in payroll month / 30). I'll confirm final numbers after forms are in.
Maya (Benefits): Medical and EAP remain US-based. For trips under or around 90 days most carriers still cover emergency care, but you should carry travel insurance for routine care and repatriation. If you plan to exceed 90 days we need to check with the carrier and possibly enroll a short-term international rider.
TaxBot: Heads up — keep a travel log. If total days in-country exceed 183 in a 12-month period you may hit local tax residency. Save copies of passport stamps and flight manifests. See gov visa guidance: https://www.thaiembassy.example/visas (not legal advice).
Priya (People Ops): Action items for @Ethan: 1) Submit Geo Move Request form link above; 2) Update Homebase travel notice and temporary homebase; 3) Attach passport pages and planned itinerary; 4) Payroll (cc @Liam) will review ADP flags. I'll confirm stipend calc by EOD Friday and post back here.
Ethan: Thanks! One more: can I ship my company monitor and keyboard to Phuket or should I bring them? Any customs paperwork needed?
Priya (People Ops): For trips >60 days we can approve equipment shipping. Please submit an Equipment Shipping Request (https://redwood.example.com/ops/equipment-shipping) and include the customs invoice and declared value. If the gear is company property we typically cover return shipping; outbound shipping may be at your expense unless pre-approved.
Liam (Payroll): If company covers shipping we need HS codes and declared values for accounting and customs. Send receipts and invoices to payroll@redwood.example.com so we can track any tax implications. No payroll withholding change expected; we won't gross-up stipend for foreign shipping.
Ethan: Got it — I'll submit forms today and attach passport scan. Thanks :thumbsup:
(25m later) Priya (People Ops): Quick follow-up: reviewed dates. Stipend calc preview: May partial (May 15-31 = 17 days) => 17/30 of monthly stipend, June = full, July = full, Aug partial (Aug 1-13 = 13 days) => 13/30. We'll split payments across the May and August payroll cycles per normal schedule.
Liam (Payroll): Confirmed. No change to tax withholding in ADP. Payroll will process the pro-rated stipend as a non-taxable reimbursement where policy allows; if customs/shipping is paid as a taxable benefit we'll notify you.
Ethan: Perfect, thanks everyone! I'll submit everything now and ping if anything changes :raised_hands:
Priya (People Ops): Thanks — leaving this thread open. We'll update once payroll and benefits confirm final notes and any paperwork required for customs.
TaxBot: Reminder set to check travel log at 30/60/90 days.
Ethan: Appreciate it — will keep detailed logs and share copies of stamps and itineraries when I submit the form.
